title: Seventh Word Proof For Patience And Reliance Weakness As A Document

questions.question: What are the two medicines mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: They are trusting Allah with patience, and relying on Allah’s power while being sure of His wisdom.

questions.question: How does the passage describe a person who knows he is weak and turns to Allah?
questions.answer: It describes him as someone who feels safe by depending on the Lord of the whole world.

questions.question: What does a believer say when a very hard trouble comes?
questions.answer: He says that he belongs to Allah and will return to Him.

questions.question: Why does the passage say such a person has less to fear?
questions.answer: Because he trusts Allah’s mercy and power instead of depending only on himself.

questions.question: What surprising idea does the passage teach about weakness and fear of Allah?
questions.answer: It teaches that they can bring a kind of sweetness and peace when they lead a person to Allah.

questions.question: What example is given to help explain this idea?
questions.answer: An example is given of a very young child who feels safest by running to his mother when he feels helpless.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does the kindness of mothers show us?
questions.answer: It shows a small sign of Allah’s much greater mercy.

questions.question: Why did wise people admit that they had no real power of their own?
questions.answer: Because they wanted to seek shelter in Allah and not be fooled by pride.

questions.question: What did wise people make into a means of drawing near to Allah?
questions.answer: They used their weakness and their fear of Allah as a way to turn to Him.

questions.question: What is the main lesson of this passage?
questions.answer: The main lesson is that a person finds peace by knowing his need for Allah and trusting Him fully.

questions.question: In this passage, what is the first medicine made of?
questions.answer: It is made of trust in Allah and patience.

questions.question: What is the second part of the two medicines in this passage?
questions.answer: It is depending on the Creator’s power and trusting His wise plan.

questions.question: How is Allah’s power shown in the passage?
questions.answer: It is shown as unlimited power that can make things happen by His command.

questions.question: When someone faces a disaster, what should he do according to the passage?
questions.answer: He should remember that he belongs to Allah and place his trust in Him.

questions.question: What kind of Lord does the passage tell the believer to trust?
questions.answer: A Lord who is full of compassion and care.

questions.question: Why might a person with knowledge of Allah find comfort even in weakness?
questions.answer: Because weakness helps him stop trusting himself and turn to Allah.

questions.question: What does the baby example teach about fear?
questions.answer: It teaches that fear can lead someone to a place of safety and tenderness.

questions.question: Is the mercy of human mothers the highest mercy described here?
questions.answer: No. It is only a tiny sign of Allah’s much greater mercy.

questions.question: What did wise people do because of this understanding?
questions.answer: They turned away from claiming strength for themselves and sought protection in Allah.

questions.question: What attitude does the passage warn against without saying it directly?
questions.answer: It warns against pride in one’s own strength and acting as if one does not need Allah.

questions.question: What two actions are called medicines in the passage?
questions.answer: Patient trust in Allah, and confidence in Allah’s power and wisdom.

questions.question: According to the passage, what should a person do with his helplessness?
questions.answer: He should use it to rely on Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage answer the question of whether these medicines really help?
questions.answer: It says clearly that they truly do help.

questions.question: Why is a person stronger when he admits his weakness before Allah?
questions.answer: Because he is then supported by Allah instead of being left to his own limited ability.

questions.question: What words of faith are mentioned for times of suffering?
questions.answer: The words that remind a person that he belongs to Allah and will return to Him.

questions.question: How can fear be good in the passage?
questions.answer: It is good when it makes a person seek safety with Allah.

questions.question: Why is the child-and-mother picture a helpful comparison?
questions.answer: Because it shows how someone small and weak finds comfort by going to one who cares for him.

questions.question: What bigger truth does the passage teach through the mother’s care?
questions.answer: That Allah’s mercy is far greater than the mercy people show each other.

questions.question: How did wise people act after learning this truth?
questions.answer: They stopped trusting their own power and took refuge in Allah.

questions.question: What feeling should this passage grow in a believer’s heart?
questions.answer: It should grow humility, trust, and closeness to Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say can heal a person spiritually like medicine?
questions.answer: Trusting Allah patiently and depending on His power and wisdom.

questions.question: What title for Allah in the passage shows His rule over everything?
questions.answer: He is presented as the ruler of the whole world.

questions.question: How does that truth help a believer during hardship?
questions.answer: It helps the believer feel calm, because Allah is able to control what people cannot control.

questions.question: What response to calamity is praised in the passage?
questions.answer: Remembering that we belong to Allah and returning to Him, while trusting Him.

questions.question: What does the passage say a person who knows Allah may feel about his own weakness?
questions.answer: He may even find peace and sweetness in it because it leads him to Allah.

questions.question: What everyday family picture is used to explain this?
questions.answer: A small child finding comfort by going to his mother.

questions.question: In that example, why does the child go to his mother?
questions.answer: Because he knows he is helpless and feels safe with her care.

questions.question: How is Allah’s mercy compared with a mother’s mercy?
questions.answer: A mother’s mercy is only a tiny reflection of Allah’s mercy.

questions.question: What did wise people strongly reject about themselves?
questions.answer: They rejected the idea that they had real strength and power on their own.

questions.question: What did they choose instead?
questions.answer: They chose to seek refuge in Allah through their weakness and fear of Him.

questions.question: Which two qualities are joined together as the first remedy in the passage?
questions.answer: Trust in Allah and patience.

questions.question: Which two things are joined together as the second remedy?
questions.answer: Leaning on the Creator’s power and being sure of His wisdom.

questions.question: What can remove fear from a person’s heart, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Depending on Allah, who has complete power over all things.

questions.question: What should a believer remember when hit by a severe test?
questions.answer: He should remember that his life belongs to Allah and that he will return to Him.

questions.question: What kind of joy can come from knowing one’s helplessness?
questions.answer: A quiet joy that comes from taking shelter with Allah.

questions.question: Why is fear of Allah not shown as something only negative here?
questions.answer: Because it can bring a person closer to Allah’s mercy and protection.

questions.question: How does the baby example make the lesson easier to understand?
questions.answer: It shows that feeling weak can lead someone to the safest place.

questions.question: What does the passage say about all mothers’ compassion together?
questions.answer: Even that is only a small glimpse of divine mercy.

questions.question: Why did wise people openly admit their weakness?
questions.answer: So they could rely on Allah instead of being proud of themselves.

questions.question: If you put the whole passage into one short teaching, what would it be?
questions.answer: Real peace comes from knowing you need Allah and turning to Him.

questions.question: In the passage, what are the two spiritual medicines given to people?
questions.answer: One is trust in Allah with patience, and the other is confidence in Allah’s power and wisdom.

questions.question: What does the passage say about Allah’s ability to make things happen?
questions.answer: It says His command is enough for things to come into being.

questions.question: Why should that truth comfort someone in a crisis?
questions.answer: Because it reminds him that Allah can handle what is impossible for people.

questions.question: What is the believer’s reaction to the hardest troubles in this passage?
questions.answer: He turns to Allah and trusts Him while remembering that he will return to Him.

questions.question: What unusual lesson does the passage give about being powerless?
questions.answer: It teaches that powerlessness can be good if it brings a person nearer to Allah.

questions.question: What feeling is connected with fear of Allah here?
questions.answer: A feeling of safety and sweetness through taking refuge in Him.

questions.question: What example from early childhood is used?
questions.answer: A baby who feels protected when going to his mother.

questions.question: Why is that example not the final point?
questions.answer: Because the passage wants us to understand that Allah’s mercy is much greater than a mother’s mercy.

questions.question: How did wise people use their weakness and fear?
questions.answer: They treated them like helpers that brought them to Allah.

questions.question: What character quality do these wise people show?
questions.answer: They show humility and deep trust in Allah.
